extracted.subtask_description: Practical laboratory procedures and standards for systematic morphological, staining, biochemical, gas and physical characterization of bacterial isolates using microscopy, culture techniques, and analytical assays. Includes sampling intervals, controls, incubation conditions, instrumentation and interpretation notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement of motile organisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure several individuals in each hanging drop by means of the eyepiece micrometer or the eikonometer, and average the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer multiple measurements per hanging drop to obtain an average. Use the eyepiece micrometer or eikonometer (see page 63) for accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation of spore formation (hanging-drop)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare hanging-drop cultivations from vegetative forms, adding a trace of magenta solution (0.5%) or other intra vitam stain to facilitate observation; select a solitary bacillus and observe spore formation using successive objectives (1/6-inch then 1/12-inch oil-immersion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a warm stage if necessary. Measure any alteration in size during spore formation by means of the Ramsden micrometer. (References: page 78, page 77, Ramsden micrometer.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation of spore germination (hanging-drop)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare hanging-drop cultivations from old cultures lacking living vegetative forms and observe the process of germination similarly to spore formation observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the same microscope objectives and staining considerations as for spore formation; observe timing and morphologic changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spore-formation sampling when hanging-drop impossible
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant organism in broth and incubate under optimum conditions; at regular intervals (e.g., every 30 minutes) remove a loopful, prepare a cover-slip film, fix while still wet in corrosive sublimate fixing solution, stain with aniline gentian violet, partially decolourise with 2% acetic acid, mount, number consecutively and examine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use systematic timed sampling and consistent fixation/staining to observe stages of spore formation across time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spore-germination sampling when hanging-drop impossible
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose a thick emulsion of spores to 80 °C for ten minutes, transfer to sterile nutrient broth and incubate; remove specimens at short intervals (e.g., five minutes), fix, stain and examine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This heat-treatment followed by timed sampling allows observation of germination stages in fixed preparations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of eye screen for prolonged observation
rubrics_metrics.description: For lengthy microscopic observations, employ an eye screen before the unused eye to enhance comfort (illustrated, Fig. 49).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A small ergonomics note to reduce eye strain during extended observation periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphology in stained preparations — shape
rubrics_metrics.description: Record the shape of organisms in stained preparations (see classification, page 131).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate staining and compare to classification references for accurate shape determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphology in stained preparations — size measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare cover-slip film preparations at various ages, fix by exposure to 115 °C for twenty minutes in a hot-air oven; stain by Gram's method (if applicable) or dilute carbol-fuchsin; measure about twenty-five individuals in each film by Ramsden's or stage micrometer and average the result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take multiple measurements to compute an average; ensure uniform fixation and staining for comparative accuracy (see page 66).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording pleomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: If pleomorphism is noted, record the predominant character of the variant forms, on what medium(s) they are observed, and at what period of development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document environment and timing to contextualize pleomorphic forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagella documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: If flagella are noted, record the method of staining, position and arrangement, and number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to flagella staining methods (page 101) and classification (page 136) for proper technique and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spore documentation in stained preps
rubrics_metrics.description: If spores are noted, record method of staining, shape, size, position within the parent cell, condition of parent cell as to shape, optimum medium and temperature, age of cultivation, environmental conditions (temperature, atmosphere), and method of germination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive record-keeping for spores to relate morphology to culture conditions and germination behavior (see page 139 and page 140).

rubrics_metrics.name: Involution form recording
rubrics_metrics.description: If involution forms are noted, record method of staining, character (e.g., living or dead), shape, on what medium they are observed, age of medium, and environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish involution forms from artifacts by noting staining behaviour and contextual culture details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metachromatic granules reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: If metachromatic granules are noted, record method of staining, character of granules, number of granules, and colour of granules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate stains and enumerate granules to aid identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gram's staining reaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Report Gram's method result as positive or negative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State Gram reaction clearly; use appropriate controls and note any atypical reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neisser's staining reaction
rubrics_metrics.description: If granules are noted by Neisser's method, record their position and number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide positional detail as well as count for diagnostic value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ziehl-Neelsen (acid-fast) reaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Report whether organisms are acid-fast or decolourised by Ziehl-Neelsen's method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include technique details and controls; note partial acid-fastness where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple aniline dyes documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Note which simple aniline dyes give the best results, with details of staining processes (e.g., methylene-blue, fuchsin, gentian violet, thionine blue and their modifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record dye, concentration and steps used so results are reproducible and comparable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare cultivations under optimum conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare all cultivations for biochemical and other examinations under optimum conditions previously determined for each organism as to reaction of medium, incubation temperature, and atmospheric environment; keep careful records and age of cultivation used in the final examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine and document 'optimum' conditions for each organism prior to biochemical testing to ensure valid results; maintain detailed logs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include control (uninoculated) medium for biochemical tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Always examine a control (uninoculated) tube or flask of medium from the same batch, kept under identical conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls are essential to interpret biochemical assays and detect medium artifacts; do not omit controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for biochemical examinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine cultivations for metabolic products after forty-eight hours' growth; if results are negative, test further cultivations at three days, five days, and ten days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated sampling across time ensures delayed metabolic activities are detected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proteolytic enzyme testing and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use filtered blood-serum or milk-serum medium; make liquid faintly acid then boil, filter, and perform copper sulphate (alkaline) test for proteose/peptone (pink -> violet), saturate filtrate with ammonium sulphate to precipitate proteose, and perform Millon's reagent (tyrosine = red) and glyoxylic acid + conc. sulphuric acid (violet ring = tryptophane) tests on fractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the stepwise fractionation and reagent reactions to distinguish proteose, peptone, tyrosine and tryptophane; note reagents required and expected colour/precipitate endpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diastase (amylase) testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use inosite-free bouillon cultures; mix cultivation with thin starch paste (2% thymol), incubate at 37 °C for 6–8 hours, filter and test filtrate for sugar with Fehling's solution (yellow/orange precipitate = sugar).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare starch paste and thymol as antiseptic; maintain boiling Fehling control and add filtrate dropwise to detect reducing sugar produced by diastase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invertase testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use inosite-free bouillon cultures; mix cultivar with carbolised cane sugar solution (2% sugar + 2% carbolic acid), allow to stand, filter and test filtrate for reducing sugar as in diastase test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect conversion of saccharose to dextrose and laevulose by same reducing-sugar assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rennin (‘lab’) enzyme testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare tube cultures in inosite-free bouillon, sterilise by heating to 55 °C for 30 minutes, inoculate three tubes of litmus milk with culture aliquots, incubate at 22 °C and examine daily for ten days; absence of coagulation at end indicates absence of rennin ferment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use litmus milk and prolonged observation to detect milk-coagulating enzymes independent of acid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fermentation reactions testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare tube cultivations on peptone water containing various percentages of carbohydrate substrates and on peptone water containing 1% of organic salts; observe day-to-day up to ten days, noting growth, reaction and gas production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a panel of carbohydrate and salt-containing media to characterize fermentative capabilities; record reaction changes and gas evolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acid production — quantitative titration
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare bulk cultivation and control, sterilise by heating, determine titre of the medium in inoculated and control flasks (using methods for estimating reaction of media); the difference gives total acid production in terms of normal NaOH. If growth is heavy, filter cultivation prior to titration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heat both inoculated and control flasks at 100 °C for 30 minutes prior to titration; filter when turbidity impedes endpoint detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acid production — qualitative identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Distil bulk cultivation (with precipitated chalk and paraffin layer to prevent frothing) to obtain distillates containing volatile acids and residues containing fixed acids; perform sequential chemical tests (baryta precipitation, alcohol extraction, ferric chloride, silver nitrate, smell, and other reactions) to identify formic, acetic, propionic, butyric, lactic, oxalic, succinic, benzoic, salicylic, gallic and tannic acids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow detailed fractionation (distillate A, residue a, filtrate B, residue b) and specific reagent tests (e.g., barium salts, ferric chloride, nitroprusside) to distinguish acids; measure volatile acid by titration of known volume if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ammonia production testing (Nessler)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare bulk nutrient bouillon cultivation and control, distil with calcined magnesia, collect 50 c.c. distillate, add 1 c.c. Nessler reagent; yellow colour indicates ammonia, with depth proportional to amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use identical treatment for control and culture; interpret colour intensity for semi-quantitative assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alcohol, acetaldehyde, acetone detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide distillate into portions and apply tests: iodoform test (iodine + NaOH) for acetaldehyde/acetone/alcohol (crystalline iodoform precipitate), Schiff's reagent for aldehyde (violet/red), potassium bichromate oxidation-distillation for alcohol (green reduction), nitroprusside/alkali with ammonium sulphate for acetone (deep permanganate colour); interpret presence/absence and relative behaviour on warming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that some tests may be absent despite odor; use multiple complementary tests for reliable identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indol production (Rosindol) testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare tube cultures (inosite-free bouillon or peptone water), remove 2 c.c. culture, add 2 c.c. paradimethylamino-benzaldehyde solution and 2 c.c. potassium persulphate; a delicate rose-pink colour indicates indol. Alternative nitrosoindol test uses concentrated acid poured down the tube to produce rose-pink/red at junction if indol (plus nitrite).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If cultures incubated at 37 °C, cool to room temperature before testing. Note alternative two-stage nitrosoindol procedure and single-stage acid + trace nitrite approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phenol production testing and separation from indol
rubrics_metrics.description: Distil acidified nutrient bouillon cultivation and test distillate fractions with Millon's reagent (red), ferric chloride (violet), and bromine water (tribromo-phenol ppt.) to detect phenol. If both indol and phenol suspected, separate by redistillation after alkaline/acid treatments to partition indol and phenol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sequential distillation, alkalinisation, CO2 saturation and redistillation to separate indol (distillate) from phenol (residue); then apply respective tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pigment production characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Grow tube cultivations on various media and incubate under varying temperature (37 °C and 20 °C), atmospheric (aerobic/anaerobic) and light (exposed/protected) conditions; note conditions most favourable to pigment formation, solubility in solvents (water, alcohol, ether, chloroform, benzol, carbon bisulphide), effects of acids and alkalies, and spectroscopic reactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record solvent solubility, pH stability and spectroscopic properties to fully characterise pigments and optimal producing conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection of reducing agent formation — colour destruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare tube cultivations in nutrient bouillon tinted with litmus, rosolic acid, neutral red and examine daily for colour change indicating reducing action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Daily monitoring of tinted media reveals reducing activity that destroys dye colour; document timing and extent of colour loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nitrates to nitrites test
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare nitrate bouillon or nitrate peptone solution cultures and control tubes; add a few drops sulphuric acid then 2–3 c.c. of metaphenylene diamine (5%); brownish-red colour = nitrites. Controls required because medium may absorb atmospheric nitrites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always compare culture tube to uninoculated control processed identically to rule out environmental contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carbon dioxide and hydrogen gas testing (fermentation tubes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inoculate fermentation tubes containing sugar bouillon, incubate, mark gas column length at 24-hour intervals and express as percentage of closed branch; to roughly determine CO2 vs H2 proportions, fill bulb with caustic soda to absorb CO2, remeasure loss in volume for CO2 and residual gas for H2; residual gas may be exploded to confirm H2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use inosite-free bouillon when required; measure with millimetre scale and perform caustic soda absorption carefully to avoid contaminating samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sulphuretted hydrogen detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Inoculate iron peptone or lead peptone solutions with culture and control tubes; observe daily for darkening of precipitate (yellowish-white -> brownish-black/jet black) proportional to amount of H2S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use control tubes to verify specificity; depth of darkening gives semi-quantitative estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative gas analysis (Pakes / Orsat-Lunge)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect gases from large Bohemian flask cultures using gas receiver (bell jar + three-way tap) immersed in mercury and sealed; when evolution has ceased, mix gases with Orsat-Lunge apparatus (mercury-operated) and analyse for CO2, O2, H2 and N2; allow for initial air volume in calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires specific apparatus (bell jar, mercury, gas tubes, Orsat-Lunge) and sealing with wax; mark mercury levels daily during incubation and permit thorough mixing prior to sampling. For anaerobic collections, prepare coupled flasks, sterilise and manipulate under vacuum/sterile conditions as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine growth under differing atmospheres
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether organism is obligate aerobe, facultative anaerobe, or obligate anaerobe by preparing sets of cultivations incubated aerobically and anaerobically in various media and apparatus (Buchner's tubes, Bulloch's apparatus, exhaust pump, pyrogallic acid and caustic soda).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare multiple sets (A–D) with combinations of agar/gelatine/bouillon and incubation temperatures (37 °C and 20 °C), seal or exhaust air as required, observe macroscopically and microscopically daily up to seven days and control results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Growth under gases other than oxygen
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Bulloch's apparatus with sterile gas filter connected to a gasometer or generator to replace air with test gas (SO2, N2O, NO, CO2 etc.); incubate under optimum temperature and examine daily, removing one tube each day to assess viability and determine exposure time required to kill organisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm complete air replacement by gas analysis of exit tube; incubate with controls and re-incubate removed tubes under optimum conditions to determine survival post-exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperature range and optimum determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare series of tube cultivations in fluid media and incubate across a series of incubators at fixed temperatures varying by 5 °C between 5 °C and 50 °C; incubate one tube per temperature and examine at half-hour intervals for 5 to 18 hours to determine range and growth characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sufficient temperature steps (every 5 °C) to identify range and optimum; where incubator numbers are limited, use water-baths for selected temperatures (e.g., thermal death-point testing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Thermal death-point testing (moist and dry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine thermal death-points for vegetative forms and spores under moist and dry conditions (separate tests for vegetative forms and spores).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standardised exposure times and temperatures, and record conditions precisely to compare susceptibility across forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess reaction of medium and resistance to lethal agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine growth and development with respect to reaction (pH) of medium; assess resistance to desiccation, light (diffuse, direct, primary colours), heat, and chemical antiseptics and disinfectants; record vitality in artificial cultures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform controlled experiments varying single parameters (pH, humidity, light spectrum, temperature, antiseptic concentration) and document organism viability under each condition.
